extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing LaTeX manuscripts for the journals Geometry & Topology and Algebraic & Geometric Topology (mathematics researchers submitting to MSP)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and house-style guidelines for preparing LaTeX source files for submission to the journals Geometry & Topology and Algebraic & Geometric Topology, including structural, stylistic, graphics, and production-related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-structured LaTeX source
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to submit articles in well-structured LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, follow the listed structural conventions (bibliography via BibTeX or standard LaTeX, proper labeling/cross-referencing of sections, theorems, figures, etc). Poorly structured files may be returned for revision because adding structure later is time-consuming and error-prone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography: standard LaTeX or BibTeX and use \cite
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography must be structured using standard LaTeX syntax or generated by BibTeX, with citations made using the \cite command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use any bibliography style for submission, but production will change it to the house style (gtart.bst). Links to gtart.bst are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label and cross-reference all numbered items
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections, subsections, figures, tables, numbered equations, etc should be labelled and cross-referenced using \label and \ref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper cross-references make reformatting easy; missing labels/cross-refs can require resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proper theorem-like environments and label them
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorems, remarks, definitions, etc must be set out using proper environments (defined with \newtheorem commands) and also labelled and cross-referenced with \label and \ref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbered environments should be structured consistently to avoid confusion when citing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures must be publication quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures, whether prepared electronically or hand-drawn, must be of publication quality; fuzzy or sloppily drawn figures will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether a figure is acceptable, contact production at graphics@msp.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a structured outline in the introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to give a structured outline of the paper in the introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a house-style preference to aid readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid \thanks; include Acknowledgements subsection
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use the \thanks field. Instead have an (sub)subsection called 'Acknowledgements' either at the end of the introduction or immediately preceding the bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the preferred placement and format for acknowledgements in G&T and AGT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered theorem-like environments should share a single counter
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered environments such as theorems, propositions, lemmas, definitions, remarks, notation, etc should all share a single counter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes it easier to find cross-references in the printed version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbering options
rubrics_metrics.description: Equations may be numbered consecutively, within sections, or in sequence with numbered environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a consistent scheme; production can renumber but consistency helps readability and citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floating material counters separate from non-floating counters
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating material (figures and tables) should not share counters with nonfloating material (theorems, definitions, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep counters distinct to avoid confusing numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: You may use \swapnumbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use \swapnumbers to reverse the order of theorem names and numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is acceptable if you prefer that style; ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid numbering conflicts between subsections and results
rubrics_metrics.description: To make it easy for others to cite your paper unambiguously, avoid numbering conflicts between subsections and results (e.g., both labeled '4.1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One suggested approach is to number subsections alphabetically (1A, 1B, ...), or number them in a sequence that avoids collisions with result numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style: include author names in citations (at least in introduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the introduction (at the least), citations should be accompanied by the names of the authors (e.g., 'We recommend Ginzburg and Weinstein \cite{ginzwein} for background reading').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't need to repeat the names if the paper has been cited recently; prefer citing specific results/definitions/sections rather than whole works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific results/sections rather than whole works
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific results, definitions, sections, etc rather than whole works whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production may ask you to supply such details if they are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and abbreviation: Guardian style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Guardian style' for punctuation: omit full stops from ie, eg, cf, etc, and other common abbreviations; omit full stops from figure or table captions that consist solely of a noun phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This streamlined style is preferred for clarity and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand most abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand most abbreviations in running text (for example, use 'see Theorem 3.7' rather than 'see Thm. 3.7'; use 'pages 47–50' rather than 'pp. 47–50').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small gains in space are less important than clarity and a notes-like appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: prepare electronically; prefer vector formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics should be prepared electronically unless completely impractical; figures should normally be vector graphics and submitted either in PDF or EPS format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics preserve quality on scaling and are preferred for production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitmap figures: produce at high resolution (>= 300 dpi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitmapped figures (e.g., JPG or PNG) should be generated at the highest possible resolution, at least 300 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-resolution bitmaps will not be acceptable for print quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure labels should be generated using LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure labels should be generated using LaTeX so that label fonts match the paper and can be edited/resized safely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pinlabel package is provided for this purpose (link to pinlabel.sty and documentation). This avoids illegible labels after resizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact production for graphics questions
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsure whether a particular figure is acceptable or for other graphics-related questions, email graphics@msp.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production staff will advise on acceptability and technical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not extensively customize layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid extensively customizing layout with explicit spacing commands (\vskip, \hspace), by altering layout parameters (\textwidth, \textheight, \pagestyle), or by using packages such as geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All such customizations will be removed during production to maintain consistent journal appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize use of external LaTeX packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The fewer external LaTeX packages you use, the better, although some are unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of relatively trouble-free packages is provided (diagrams, amscd, xy, tikz-cd, tikz, pgfplots, pinlabel, geompsfi, slashed, pifont, stmaryrd). Avoid obscure or problematic packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using gtpart.cls is optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who wish may use the public class file gtpart.cls to format their article before submitting source files; using it is completely optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't use it, production will convert your source files to gtpart.cls during production. Template and further instructions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv reference field for submissions deposited on arXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article has been deposited on the arXiv, fill out the \arxivreference{} field in the template with its reference number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newer-style reference numbers with a period, include only the number (e.g., 1604.00199). For older numbers without a period, include the prefix (e.g., math/0305071). Do not include the 'arXiv:' prefix for newer-style numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography house style and gtart.bst
rubrics_metrics.description: The house BibTeX style file gtart.bst is available and will be used in production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are free to use any style for submission, but production will change it to gtart.bst. A link to download gtart.bst is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article mockup usage and distribution restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: By adding one of \gtart, \agtart or \gtmonart you can make gtpart.cls produce a full mockup of a published article using the journal running heads/feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place your article in mockup form in a public place (e.g., arXiv) unless it has been accepted for publication in the relevant journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final checks and warnings about package interactions and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting your article to the class file, check carefully that all symbols are displayed as intended because there may be unpredictable interactions between gtpart.cls and external packages. Production uses commercial fonts that are not identical to those used by gtpart.cls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect differences in page and line breaks between your prepared file and the published version; verify symbol rendering before submission to avoid surprises.
